newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICA wins contracts for Pemex's Cactus plant.
newsitem.headline: ICA wins contracts for Pemex's Cactus plant.

text.p: Empresas ICA won two contracts worth 297 million pesos for reconstruction of part of Pemex's Cactus natural gas plant, which was damaged in an explosion on July 26, ICA said.

In a statement, ICA said that "Pemex Gas and Basic Petrochemicals awarded to ICA Fluor Daniel two contracts for a total of 297 million pesos related to the reconstruction of the Criogenic 1 plant and related services," the company said.

Work will focus on the criogenic plant #1 that was heavily damaged in the July blast and in auxiliary services in the production of natural gas. ICA said the work will raise production at the facility by 25 percent.
"The work...will be completed under a 'fast-track' program that will last nine months, with the planned building work finished by April 1997," ICA said.
Another criogenic plant, #2, was completely destroyed in the blast. That unit will probably need to be rebuilt entirely and will likely be contracted out by Pemex in the near future, ICA said.
Cactus was Pemex's largest gas-producing facility. Mexico was forced to import natural gas for about a month after the blast. It has also been importing propane gas.
ICA Flour Daniel is a joint venture between Empresas ICA S.A. and Flour Daniel Inc.
